dedupe_keys.name: dhs program service provision assessment spa health facility surveys

description: The Service Provision Assessment is a health facility survey run by the Demographic and Health Surveys Program with national ministries of health, collecting data on service availability and quality of care in a country's health system. It assesses a wide range of services with a focus on antenatal care, family planning, maternity care and sick child services, and measures quality in two dimensions: structural quality, meaning physical and human resources such as infrastructure, equipment, medicines and staff, and process quality, meaning how care is provided and experienced. The survey was redesigned in 2022 with experts from WHO, UNICEF and ministries of health. Coverage is the participating low and middle income countries, each surveyed in particular years, typically as a census or representative sample of facilities with GPS locations where released. Final reports are free, and facility, provider and client datasets are free to download after registering a research project with the DHS Program. Caveats: surveys are infrequent and not every country takes part, facility coordinates may be restricted, and questionnaires changed with the redesign. Simulation uses: parameterising health facility readiness, including power, water and equipment, in healthcare disruption models, and comparing service availability across regions. Related records: the WHO Harmonized Health Facility Assessment (data-who-harmonized-health-facility-assessment-hhfa) is a related standard survey and the GHDx catalogue (data-ghdx-global-health-data-exchange) lists such surveys.
